scope.definition_identification: Local rule IDs introduced upstream relative to the common base; final merged paths include the item-taxonomy relocations.

validation.limitation: Syntax, graph, mechanical policy, severity fixtures and performance pass. These checks do not establish semantic placement, binding, attack admission or product identity.

acceptance_contract: Every child refines its parent on one evidence-supported axis.
Required evidence decides tier, result and most specific home.
Imports, names and schemas do not establish product identity or exports.
Theft requires acquisition/content plus a send; multi-item requires each independent exported item.
A move preserves matching scope; a detection correction is separately tested and recorded.

findings.finding: Stolen-item admission is missing required exports
findings.violation: The required evidence is collector-method names, wallet names, Login Data or credential JSON fields. None requires a send. The multi-item rules also do not require two independent exported item families. The password placement is therefore not justified by the serialized password field alone.
findings.required_correction: Retain method, target and schema observations in their neutral homes. Admit an exfiltration composite only after requiring acquisition plus a send; classify the exported item rather than a referenced store. Remove or replace unsupported umbrella convictions.

findings.finding: Host report and DNS export claims exceed the required evidence
findings.violation: The Telegram composite requires a bot host, send-message syntax, token-assignment syntax and an encoded query, but no host/user source. The DNS regex requires hostname(), process.env.USER and oast.fun text, but no resolver or send operation.
findings.required_correction: Use neutral messaging and endpoint-construction observations for the present matchers, or bind the claimed host/user content to the send. Then use stealer/system-info for the item export rather than transport as the primary class.

findings.finding: A transferred credential database is still classified by acquisition source
findings.violation: The required NTDS acquisition plus archive/cloud upload establishes an export. TAXONOMY.md gives an admitted acquisition-to-send chain to the stolen item, not the acquisition store.
findings.required_correction: Move the export composite to objectives/exfiltration/stealer/credential/record. Keep its acquisition atoms at their source homes.

findings.finding: Benign syslog observations remain in a denial-of-service objective
findings.violation: These atoms match a stdin read, a remote_hosts identifier and syslogd wording. None establishes flooding, resource exhaustion or an attacker goal. Their use by an exception does not authorize objective placement.
findings.required_correction: Place the stdin operation and source naming observations in their corresponding neutral subjects, and retarget the existing exception.

findings.finding: Build metadata is filed as supply-chain behavior
findings.violation: An include_str! checksum filename and a SHA-256 source binding establish source/build properties. Neither requires an install hook or supply-chain trust abuse.
findings.required_correction: Place the individual source observations by their syntax/property. Reference those facts from an objective only when its other required evidence admits a supply-chain claim.

findings.finding: Generic extension capabilities are filed as deception components
findings.violation: The first rule is an OR of ordinary GPU queries. The second is an OR of a user-service command and a child-process spawn. Neither requires deception or even a VS Code extension. Component criticality does not repair placement, and both represent useful standalone observations.
findings.required_correction: Reference the existing capability atoms directly from consumers, or retain honest neutral groups with one supported result. Keep extension context and attack admission in the objective.

findings.finding: HTML title and heading properties are filed as masquerade
findings.violation: The matchers recognize title/heading copy. Genuine product pages and ordinary Drive headings satisfy them; no conflicting identity or deceptive relationship is required.
findings.required_correction: Keep title/heading observations in a neutral document or display-copy home. Require the deceptive relationship in the masquerade composite.

findings.finding: A PHP setup path is filed as a phishing kit
findings.violation: The only condition is a setup/install directory or PHP basename. This is a path property, not credential capture, impersonation or kit identity.
findings.required_correction: Use the canonical neutral filename/path observation and retarget exclusions; do not use component or baseline severity to retain a phishing feature.

findings.finding: Direction is asserted for symmetric byte transforms
findings.violation: The IDs/descriptions say decoder, the parent says encode, and the byte-loop matchers do not establish either direction. XOR and addition alone cannot decide which representation is input or output.
findings.required_correction: Name the observed transform honestly and use a direction-neutral encoding/transform home, or require evidence establishing decoding. Use the XOR scheme when required; do not retain a contradictory custom encoder placement.

findings.finding: Shader filenames choose a decoding hierarchy
findings.violation: The import atom accepts any import path containing shader/glsl. The other atom accepts an arbitrary exported call with a TVp-prefixed string. Neither proves a decoder or a shader algorithm, and the composite does not bind the imported name to the called function. Carrier/spelling is not the required scheme axis.
findings.required_correction: Keep imports and call-argument syntax as their neutral observations. Require a bound decoding operation and place it by the proven scheme, not shader origin.

findings.finding: Generic pub/sub calls are classified as NATS
findings.violation: The regexes require only .Publish("...") or .Subscribe("..."). They establish no NATS receiver or import. A consuming composite checking NATS does not change the atoms' identity.
findings.required_correction: Place the call syntax in metadata/lang/source/syntax/call/arguments or strengthen each atom with NATS binding. Preserve the benign Redis control.

findings.finding: Raw Wasm byte patterns assert an exploit and engine limit
findings.violation: The raw regexes are not restricted to parsed instructions or a validated br_table immediate. The large low-byte run can occur in data. No engine/version, vulnerable JIT transformation, overflow or sandbox boundary crossing is required. A large encoded count alone establishes neither an engine limit nor an exploit.
findings.required_correction: Recognize validated instruction/count properties separately. Require the actual exploit mechanism before assigning an exploit objective; keep raw layout evidence in metadata.

findings.finding: Dependency and helper references are treated as product identity
findings.violation: An artifact importing @cypress, referring to a helper, declaring a plovr dependency or mentioning plovr.jar need not be that library/tool. The Plovr OR inherits the same issue.
findings.required_correction: Use metadata/import, metadata/package/dependencies/manifest/identity and specific reference/path observations. Product identity needs evidence that the analyzed artifact implements the product.

findings.finding: Mutable names are accepted as benign product identity
findings.violation: The Chutes rules use names/paths plus size only. The Capium exception can match solely a chosen directory name. Names do not identify implementation, and an attacker-controlled name must not independently authorize a benign-context suppression.
findings.required_correction: Record names as metadata. Require independent content/verified provenance for product identity and for any suppressing exception.

findings.finding: An encrypted relocation payload is insufficient Expiro identity
findings.violation: The required evidence is an encrypted relocation payload profile and absent signature, with GetProcAddress or directory enumeration as alternatives. The rule does not require infection behavior or a family-specific fingerprint.
findings.required_correction: Keep the observed layout and APIs at their neutral or admitted behavioral homes. Add a distinctive, verified family fingerprint before identifying Expiro.
